'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2020–21 United States election protests]]
**[[January 6 United States Capitol attack]]
***Thousands of [[Trumpism|pro-Trump]] protesters [[2021 United States Capitol attack|storm]] the [[United States Capitol]], causing it to be evacuated. [[Washington, D.C.]] [[Mayor of the District of Columbia|mayor]] [[Muriel Bowser]] proclaimed a citywide nighttime curfew. Shots were fired, and at least six people were injured. A woman died from [[Killing of Ashli Babbitt|gunshot wounds]] by Police, according to police. Multiple members of Congress called this an attempted ''[[coup d'état]]''. The [[FBI]], police, and [[United States National Guard|National Guard]] from [[Maryland]], [[Virginia]], and D.C. itself were deployed to stop the riot. [[Smoke bomb]]s and [[pepper spray]] were also used. Multiple suspected pipe bombs were reported, including at the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]] headquarters. [https://news.yahoo.com/explosive-device-found-rnc-suspicious-211307027.html (''Yahoo! News'')] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/dc-md-va/2021/01/06/dc-protests-trump-rally-live-updates/ (''The Washington Post'')] [https://www.cnn.com/politics/live-news/congress-electoral-college-vote-count-2021/h_eed8c8ac9a408646998937a9da353acf (CNN)] [https://wrex.com/2021/01/06/nbc-person-shot-at-us-capitol-has-died/ (WREX-TV)]
***[[President pro tempore of the United States Senate|U.S President pro tempore]] [[Chuck Grassley]] announces that the [[United States Senate]] has entered recess as Senator [[James Lankford]] ([[Republican Party (United States)|R]]-[[Oklahoma|OK]]) was given out a speech, with an aide informing Lankford that [[Demonstrations in support of Donald Trump|pro-Trump]] protesters were entering the building. Additionally, the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]] enters a recess. [https://www.businessinsider.com/house-senate-go-into-recess-amid-trump-supporter-protests-2021-1 (Business Insider)] [https://www.koco.com/article/we-do-not-encourage-what-happened-today-lankford-delivers-powerful-speech-following-chaos-in-dc/35144032 (KOCO-TV)]
***The [[United States Senate chamber]] and [[Speaker of the United States House of Representatives|House Speaker]] [[Nancy Pelosi]]'s office are also breached by pro-Trump protesters. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/capitol-breached-protesters/story?id=75081629 (ABC News)] [https://www.wivb.com/news/demonstrators-invade-offices-of-lawmakers-inside-u-s-capitol/ (WIVB-TV)]
***[[President-elect of the United States|President-elect]] [[Joe Biden]] says "It's not a protest, it's an [[insurrection]]", and calls on [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] to "demand an end to this siege" by his followers. In response, President Trump released a video saying, "These are the things and events that happen when a sacred landslide election victory is so unceremoniously & viciously stripped away from great patriots who have been badly & unfairly treated for so long. Go home with love & in peace. Remember this day forever!" [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-55568830 (BBC News)] [https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/tweets-january-6-2021]
***At least seven Democratic members of Congress, including [[Ilhan Omar]], [[Ayanna Pressley]] and [[Seth Moulton]], and [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Governor of Vermont|Vermont Governor]] [[Phil Scott]], call for Trump's immediate resignation or [[impeachment|impeachment and removal]] by Congress, when it can reconvene, for [[insurrection]] against the [[United States]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-election-2020/trump-impeachment-ilhan-omar-us-capitol-b1783535.html (''The Independent'')] [https://www.wgbh.org/news/politics/2021/01/06/markey-congress-will-overwhelmingly-reject-treasonous-challenge-to-bidens-win (WGBH-TV)] [https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/archive/2021/01/impeach-trump-again/617573/ (''The Atlantic'')] [https://www.thewrap.com/vermonts-gop-governor-calls-for-trumps-removal-rep-ilhan-omar-to-draft-impeachment-articles/ (''The Wrap'')]
***The [[United States Capitol Police]] says that the Capitol was secured by 6 p.m. The Electoral College certificates were also secured. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2021/01/06/electoral-votes-were-whisked-away-pro-trump-capitol-rioters/6572383002/ (''USA Today'')] [https://www.foxcarolina.com/news/capitol-complex-secure-after-violent-occupation/article_3d9b7688-5072-11eb-a0c7-97a007ac88a6.html (WHNS-TV)]
***Three more people die during the United States Capitol riots during "separate medical emergencies", bringing the total death toll to four. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/01/06/politics/us-capitol-lockdown/index.html (CNN)]
***[[Stephanie Grisham]] resigns as the [[Chief of Staff to the First Lady of the United States|Chief of Staff]] to the [[First Lady of the United States|First Lady]] as a result of the riots. [[Matt Pottinger]] resigns as [[Deputy National Security Advisor|deputy national security adviser]]; [[Mick Mulvaney]], former [[White House Chief of Staff|chief of staff]], resigns from his remaining duties as [[United States Special Envoy for Northern Ireland|special envoy to Northern Ireland]] and [[Anna Cristina Niceta Lloyd|Anna Cristina Niceta]] resigns as [[White House Social Secretary|White House social secretary]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/06/politics/stephanie-grisham-white-house-resign/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/06/politics/national-security-adviser-resigns-trump-protest/index.html (CNN<sup>2</sup>)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Israel's role in the Syrian Civil War]]
***[[Israel]] launches airstrikes against [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps|IRGC]] and [[Hezbollah]] bases near [[Damascus]], [[Syria]]. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2021/01/07/Israel-strikes-area-south-of-Syrian-capital-Damascus (Al Arabiya)] [https://yalibnan.com/2021/01/07/israel-targets-iranian-irgc-bases-and-hezbollah-in-news-syria-strike/ (Ya Libnan)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China|COVID-19 pandemic in China]]
****Members of the [[World Health Organization]] investigating the origins of the pandemic are denied entry into [[People's Republic of China|China]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/1/6/very-disappointed-whos-covid-experts-blocked-from-china (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 8,854 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 788,402. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5323315/update-corona-indonesia-6-januari-rekor-8854-kasus-baru (detikHealth)]
****[[Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs (Indonesia)|Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs]] [[Airlangga Hartarto]] announces two-week restrictions in parts of the islands of [[Java]] and [[Bali]] beginning January 11. These restrictions include limiting operating hours for malls, an advisory for 75% of workers to [[work from home]], and capacity restrictions for restaurants and places of worship. [https://economy.okezone.com/read/2021/01/06/320/2339825/daftar-pembatasan-kegiatan-mulai-11-25-januari-wfh-75-hingga-mal-tutup-pukul-19-00 (Okezone.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Tokyo]] claims a record 1,591 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed cases in the [[Prefectures of Japan|prefecture]] to 66,343. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/01/06/national/1500-record-corona-cases/ (''The Japan Times'')]
****Nationwide, a record of more than 6,000 new cases are reported in the past 24 hours. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20210106_43/amp.html (NHK World)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record 2,593 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 125,438. [https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2021/01/06/malaysia-records-new-daily-high-of-2593-covid-19-cases-965-from-selangor/1937918 (''Malay Mail'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
****The [[Czech Republic]] reports a record of 17,278 new cases in the past 24 hours, 7,965 of which are from [[Prague]], bringing the nationwide total of cases to 776,967. [https://www.praguemorning.cz/czech-republic-report-highest-daily-number-of-covid-19-cases-since-pandemic-outbreak-2/ (Prague Morning)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Denmark]]
****[[Denmark]] bans travel to non-residents from [[South Africa]] over concerns of the [[Lineage B.1.351|501.V2 variant]]. [https://www.thelocal.dk/20210106/denmark-bans-travel-from-south-africa-over-new-virus-strain/ (The Local)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] reports a record 7,836 new cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 121,154. [https://www.independent.ie/irish-news/coronavirus-ireland-record-7836-new-cases-and-17-further-deaths-confirmed-as-schools-to-close-and-construction-to-be-halted-until-january-31-39939563.html (Independent.ie)]
****The [[Government of Ireland|government]] also agrees to tighten the [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] measures including keeping schools closed but allowing [[Leaving Certificate (Ireland)|Leaving Cert]] students to attend three days per week and also suspending non-essential construction projects. These measures will remain in place until the end of January. [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/politics/covid-19-cabinet-agrees-to-keep-schools-closed-for-january-in-most-challenging-phase-of-all-1.4451482 (''The Irish Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malta]]
****[[Malta]] reports a record of 224 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours. [https://timesofmalta.com/articles/view/new-covid-19-cases-hit-daily-record-of-224.843156 (''Times of Malta'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****The [[Netherlands]] begins a [[vaccination]] programme against [[COVID-19]] with a nurse becoming the first person to be vaccinated with [[Pfizer]]'s [[Tozinameran]] vaccine. [https://www.rtlnieuws.nl/nieuws/nederland/artikel/5206962/coronavaccin-sanna-eerste-prik-coronavirus-covid-19 (RTL Nieuws)] [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/nurse-first-in-netherlands-to-get-covid-19-vaccination/46263950 (Swiss Info)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a record of 10,027 new daily cases, bringing the nationwide cumulative total of confirmed cases to 446,606. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/310_DGS_boletim_20210106.pdf (DGS)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in San Marino]]
****[[San Marino]] announces that bars and restaurants will close at 5 p.m. until January 15, and that a curfew will begin at 10 p.m. local time. [https://www.sanmarinortv.sm/news/politica-c2/orario-ridotto-in-bar-e-ristoranti-coprifuoco-alle-22-cosa-succede-a-san-marino-dal-7-gennaio-a199332 (San Marino TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
****[[Slovenia]] reports a record of 3,354 cases in the past 24 hours. The country also surpasses 130,000 total cases. [https://www.rtvslo.si/zdravje/novi-koronavirus/v-torek-3354-okuzb-med-pcr-testi-kar-37-4-odstotka-pozitivnih/548025 (RTVSLO)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports a record 62,322 new cases of COVID-19 and a further 1,041 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]]. This is the first time since April that the daily death toll has exceeded 1,000. Major outbreaks are declared at hospitals in [[Surrey]] and [[Sussex]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55565254 (BBC News)]
***The [[European Medicines Agency]] approves the emergency use of [[Moderna]]'s [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/01/06/european-regulator-approves-moderna-covid-vaccine-for-use-in-the-eu.html (CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Morocco]]
*****[[Morocco]] approves [[AstraZeneca]]'s [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/africa/morocco-approves-use-of-astrazeneca-covid-19-vaccine/2021/01/06/2b7ef916-5068-11eb-a1f5-fdaf28cfca90_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Senegal]]
****[[President of Senegal|President]] [[Macky Sall]] declares a [[state of emergency]] and imposes a curfew at 9:00 p.m. local time in [[Dakar]] and [[Thiès]] in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20210106-senegal-declares-state-of-emergency-curfew-to-combat-spike-in-covid-19-africa-health (RFI)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec]]
****[[Premier of Quebec|Premier]] [[François Legault|Francois Legault]] announces a curfew from 8:00 p.m. until 5:00 a.m. [[Eastern Time|EST]] for whole [[Quebec|province]] except the [[Nord-du-Quebec]] administrative region from January 9 until February 8. Pharmacies and gas stations will be permitted to remain open during curfew hours. [https://montreal.ctvnews.ca/quebec-issues-province-wide-curfew-starting-saturday-in-effort-to-combat-surging-covid-19-cases-1.5256257 (CFCF-DT)]

***[[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
****Health officials in [[Australia]] announce that the country will bring forward their [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccination]] rollout plans by two weeks to early March. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-australia/australia-to-bring-forward-covid-19-vaccine-rollout-plans-idUSL1N2JG2I9 (Reuters)]

***[[Uruguay]] reports a record 946 new confirmed cases in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 23,048. [https://www.gub.uy/sistema-nacional-emergencias/comunicacion/comunicados/informe-situacion-sobre-coronavirus-covid-19-uruguay-06012021 (gob.uy)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Israel–Sudan normalization agreement]]
**[[Sudan]] formally signs the [[Abraham Accords]] as part of an agreement to normalize relations with [[Israel]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-sudan-usa-israel/sudan-quietly-signs-abraham-accords-weeks-after-israel-deal-idUKKBN29B2YK?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong national security law]]
**[[Hong Kong Police]] arrest 53 [[Pro-democracy camp (Hong Kong)|pro-democracy]] activists and politicians for [[criminal charges]] under the national security law. Those arrested include [[James To]] and [[Lam Cheuk-ting]] of the [[Democratic Party (Hong Kong)|Democratic Party]], activist [[Lester Shum]], and  [[Leung Kwok-hung]] and [[Jimmy Sham]] of the [[League of Social Democrats]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-security-idUSKBN29B01K (Reuters)] [https://news.rthk.hk/rthk/en/component/k2/1568852-20210106.htm (RTHK)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-55555299 (BBC News)] {{ill|Kickstart Wan Chai|zh|灣仔起步}} announces to disband, effective immediately. [https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/law-and-crime/article/3116854/national-security-law-stunned-crackdown-hong-kong (SCMP)]
*[[2020 Mississippi flag referendum]]
**The [[Mississippi State Senate]] passes a bill to make the [[Flag of Mississippi|state flag]] chosen in the November referendum official. The [[Mississippi House of Representatives]] passed the bill on Tuesday. [https://apnews.com/article/mississippi-bills-tate-reeves-afbe916946e4b38cb29469fe0ec7cdc4 (AP)]
*[[Killing of Breonna Taylor]]
**The [[Louisville Metro Police Department]] announces the firing of Myles Cosgrove and Joshua Jaynes, the two officers involved in the botched raid of [[Breonna Taylor]]'s home. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/breonna-taylor-shooting-louisville-police-officers-fired/ (CBS News)]
*A judge in the [[United Kingdom]] denies bail to [[WikiLeaks]] founder [[Julian Assange]] days after his extradition to the [[United States]] was blocked. The judge cited the risk of Assange escaping the extradition process or refusing to surrender to court if asked to do so. Assange's lawyers will appeal the decision whereas the [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Department of Justice]] continues to seek his extradition. Assange's partner urges the US to pardon him.  [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-wikileaks-assange/wikileaks-assange-denied-bail-by-london-court-over-risk-he-might-abscond-again-idUSKBN29B00E (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020 United States elections]]
**[[2020 United States Senate elections]]
***[[2020–21 United States Senate election in Georgia]], [[2020–21 United States Senate special election in Georgia]]
****News networks project that [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] [[Raphael Warnock]] will defeat [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Kelly Loeffler]], making him the state's first [[List of African-American United States senators|African-American Senator]]. Warnock claims victory, while Loeffler refuses to [[Concession (politics)|concede]] the race and vows to "fight on". [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/01/05/georgia-senate-runoff-election-results-kelly-loeffler-raphael-warnock.html (CNBC)] [https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/ryancbrooks/georgia-senate-democrat-raphael-warnock-wins (''BuzzFeed News'')]
****The [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] will take control of the Senate after [[Jon Ossoff]] defeated Republican [[David Perdue]], leaving incoming [[Vice President–elect of the United States|Vice President]] [[Kamala Harris]] with the tiebreaking vote. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/06/politics/ossoff-perdue-georgia-election-news/index.html (CNN)] 
**[[2021 United States Electoral College vote count]]
***A joint session of the [[United States Congress]] attempts to certify the [[United States Electoral College|Electoral College]] vote results and affirm the election of [[Joe Biden]] before being interrupted by the [[2021 storming of the United States Capitol|storming of the US Capitol]]. [https://www.cnn.com/politics/live-news/congress-electoral-college-vote-count-2021/ (CNN)]
***[[Vice President of the United States|U.S. Vice President]] [[Mike Pence]] releases a statement stating that he won't [[Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election#January 6 joint session|reject]] electoral college votes despite pressure from President Trump and his allies to do so. He reaffirms that his role in the Congressional joint session is ceremonial. [https://www.npr.org/sections/congress-electoral-college-tally-live-updates/2021/01/06/953995808/pence-says-he-doesnt-have-power-to-reject-electoral-votes (NPR)]
***Senator [[Ted Cruz]] and [[United States House of Representatives|Rep.]] [[Paul Gosar]] object to the state of [[Arizona]], making it the first time a vote is forced to accept or reject the objection since 2004, when Rep. [[Stephanie Tubbs Jones]] and Senator [[Barbara Boxer]] objected to [[George W. Bush]]'s victory in [[Ohio]] against [[John Kerry]]. The objection failed 6-93 in the Senate and 121-303 in the House. [https://www.nationalreview.com/corner/cruz-and-gosar-object-to-arizonas-electoral-votes/ (National Review)] [https://ktvz.com/politics/2021/01/06/gop-challenges-arizona-electoral-votes-the-first-of-several-expected-objections-to-bidens-2020-win/ (KTVZ-TV)] [https://www.gwinnettdailypost.com/cnn/cnn_politics/house-and-senate-reject-objection-to-arizona-electoral-votes-after-riot-at-the-capitol/article_4f40576a-631d-525e-a4fc-ff69eb0f4609.html (''Gwinnett Daily Post'')]
***Lawmakers say that they will continue certification of Biden's victory tonight. [https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/533008-lawmakers-say-they-expect-work-certifying-biden-win-to-continue-tonight (''The Hill'')]
*[[Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**The [[European Union]] withdraws their recognition of [[Juan Guaidó]] as the interim [[President of Venezuela]], instead resolving to delegate to individual member states to make their own decisions on who to recognize. [https://www.europapress.es/internacional/noticia-ue-deja-reconocer-guaido-presidente-interino-20210106123139.html (''Europapress'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Donald Trump on social media]], [[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[Twitter]] locks the personal account of President [[Donald Trump]] for the first time, citing the president's "incitement to violence", and "false claims about the results of the 2020 U.S. presidential election". The [[social media]] site warns that further attempts to violate the company's rules could result in a permanent suspension of Trump's account. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/01/06/twitter-pledges-action-on-any-calls-for-violence-in-capitol-riot.html (CNBC)]
**[[Facebook]] locks President Trump's account for 24 hours in response to the violence in [[Washington, D.C.]]. In a blog post, the social media site says today's events are an "emergency" for the platform and will be rolling out new rules in response. [https://techcrunch.com/2021/01/06/facebook-stormthecapitol-hashtag-dangerous-organizations-policy/ (TechCrunch)]
